meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hey', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hey, put on shoe covers immediately!
Hey, what's wrong?
Hey, come here!

meanings.en: to put on (an item of clothing)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put on (clothes)', paired with 'надевать'.

examples.trans: Hey, put on shoe covers immediately!
So that you do not do anything foolish!
Put the jacket on.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'shoe covers' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hey, put on shoe covers immediately!

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть бахилы.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always shoe covers.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Hey, put on shoe covers immediately!
Senechka, open the door for me immediately!
Young man, vacate the ward immediately!
